source.body: ### Bug Description The Sort node does not correctly sort numeric values when using the following configuration: Type: Simple Order: Descending When sorting numbers in descending order, the output is incorrect. However, changing the order to Ascending produces the expected results. This suggests that there may be an issue specifically with the descending numeric sorting implementation. ### To Reproduce 1. Add a Sort node to a workflow. 2. Set Type to Simple. 3. Select a numeric field to sort by. 4. Set Order to Descending. 5. Execute the workflow and inspect the output. ### Expected behavior Numeric values should be sorted from highest to lowest when Descending is selected. ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.47.7 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 26.13.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: postgres - executionMode: scaling (single-main) - concurrency: -1 - license: enterprise (production) - consumerId: e1a0c650-5177-4ea0-8974-f13a169c1ba4 ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: database ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (windows nt 10.0; win64; x64; rv:160.0) gecko/20100101 firefox/160.0 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 2 - versions: 2.47.7 - instances: - instanceKey: 7f0c62b3-f669-417f-b372-4a705e3255c6, hostId: main-eddc9af53b9d, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.47.7 - instanceKey: f19e5e12-cbb4-475d-b236-4cf9a1b42680, hostId: worker-8361d7e42714, instanceType: worker, instanceRole: unset, version: 2.47.7 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-11-13T15:11:24.588Z ### Operating System Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS ### n8n Version 2.47.7 ### Node.js Version 26.13.0 ### Database PostgreSQL ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting self hosted

comments.author: goutham-valugula
comments.text: Could you share a few input values and the output, including whether the field values are JSON numbers or strings? The Simple sorter uses `lodash/lt` for comparisons: numbers compare numerically, but numeric strings compare lexicographically (for example, "9" sorts after "10" ascending). That distinction, plus the exact field path, would help narrow down whether this is input typing or the descending-order handling.

comments.author: lowik2005
comments.text:
When the field values are JSON numbers, both ascending and descending sorting work correctly.

However, when the field values are strings:

- **Ascending** sorting works correctly, sorting values numerically as if they were numbers.
- **Descending** sorting does not work correctly, as values are compared lexicographically (for example, `"9"` is sorted after `"10"`).

This issue occurs only when using string values with descending sorting.

P.S.: I wouldn't have paid much attention to this issue, but this exact workflow using the Sort node is part of the n8n Quickstart training program. :-)
